title: Shape Areas
statement:
Work out the area of a mix of shapes through one shared shape type. Every shape can report its area, and circles and squares each compute it their own way.

The first line is a count `n` (it can be 0). Each of the next `n` lines is a shape: `circle r` for a circle with radius `r`, or `square s` for a square with side `s`. Sizes are decimal numbers, 0 or more.

Print the area of each shape on its own line, in input order, then a last line `Total: ` followed by the sum of all the areas. Print every number with exactly 2 decimal places. A circle's area is pi times `r` squared, using the full value of pi (not `3.14`), and a square's area is `s` squared. Add up the full areas and round only when you print, so the total can differ from the sum of the printed lines. With no shapes, print only `Total: 0.00`.

Input:

```text
3
circle 1
square 2
circle 2.5
```

Expected output:

```text
3.14
4.00
19.63
Total: 26.78
```
hints: Each shape class only needs to know its own formula. Fill in one area method per class.
The total does not care which kind each shape is. Loop over the shapes and ask each one for its area.
